lines.japanese: 歩行速度と目的地までの道筋を調整して、狙い通り二時間目と三時間目のあいだに学校へ着いた。
lines.english: Adjusting my walking speed and route, I arrive at school between second and third period, just as planned.

lines.japanese: いくら本調子に近付いたとはいえ、わざわざ授業途中の静けさへ闖入してゆくほどの勇気はまだない。全校中が休み時間を迎えて程良くざわめいているこの隙に、さりげなく教室へ潜りこんでしまおう。
lines.english: However close I am to feeling normal, I'm not yet brave enough to deliberately invade the silence of a class in progress. While the whole school is on break, with a comfortable buzz of noise, I'll slip into the classroom unnoticed.

lines.japanese: オフィス街の端にそびえる地上７階建てのビル校舎。その冷たい威容を、ふもとから見上げて深呼吸した。
lines.english: A seven-story school building towers at the edge of the office district. I look up at its cold, imposing bulk from below and take a deep breath.

lines.japanese: 「よし、がんばるな。普通に普通に」
lines.english: “Okay. Don't try too hard. Just normal, normal.”

lines.japanese: 手首をぷらぷら回しながら自己暗示。
lines.english: I roll my wrists loosely, talking myself into it.

lines.japanese: 活動機能が上がってきたからと言って楽観はできない。次に懸念されるのがリバウンドだ。抑圧されていた交感神経が、反動でかえって働きすぎてしまうとまた面倒なことになる。
lines.english: Even if my ability to function is rising, I can't be optimistic. The next worry is a rebound. If the suppressed sympathetic nerves overreact and start working too hard, things become troublesome again.

lines.japanese: 「行きます」
lines.english: “Here I go.”

lines.japanese: 私は昼の分の薬を呑みくだして校門を越えた。
lines.english: I swallow my midday medicine and pass through the school gates.

lines.japanese: 休み時間の喧騒に紛れてさりげなく教室へ、という小さな野望の前に障害が立ちふさがった。
lines.english: An obstacle rises before my modest ambition to slip into the classroom amid the noise of the break.

lines.japanese: 校門から昇降口、玄関ロビー、エレベーターと経て、順調に７階廊下へ出たときだ。
lines.english: I've made my way smoothly from the gate to the shoe-changing entrance, through the lobby, up the elevator, and out into the seventh-floor hallway.

lines.japanese: 私を呼びとめたのは、朝にも見かけたクラス委員長。羽田……君？　下の名前はタカシ、だったかな。
lines.english: The one who stops me is the class president I saw this morning. Hane... da? Was his first name Takashi?

lines.japanese: 「うん、大丈夫だよ……うん……うん、頭痛とかはないの」
lines.english: “Yeah, I'm okay... Yeah... Yeah, no headache or anything.”

lines.japanese: 彼の学級委員としての責務──遅刻者の体調を気遣ったいくつかの質問に、私は真摯に対応した。
lines.english: I respond sincerely to the questions that come with his duty as class president: concern for a late student's health.

lines.japanese: 私の記憶が正しければ、羽田君はいわれもなく積極的に他人へ声をかけるようなタイプじゃなかったはず。きっと担任あたりから言いつかったのだろう。
lines.english: If I remember right, Haneda isn't the sort to go out of his way to talk to people for no reason. Our homeroom teacher probably told him to.

lines.japanese: 同情を禁じ得ない。私には分かる。彼のような人間にとって、話したくもない相手と話すことを強要されるのは、地味に精神を疲弊する作業のはずだ。
lines.english: I can't help feeling sorry for him. I understand. For someone like him, being forced to talk to someone he doesn't want to talk to must quietly wear him down.

lines.japanese: 「大変だね、委員長」
lines.english: “Being class president is hard, huh?”

lines.japanese: 思わず口をついて出てしまった。
lines.english: It slips out before I know it.

lines.japanese: きょとんと目を丸くする羽田君。
lines.english: Haneda's eyes widen in puzzlement.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ううん、心配してくれてありがとう」
lines.english: “Oh, no. Thank you for worrying about me.”

lines.japanese: たとえ本意でなくとも、誰かから気にかけてもらえることは存外嬉しいものだ。
lines.english: Even if they don't really mean it, someone taking an interest in you is surprisingly nice.

lines.japanese: しかも彼は、義務的な態度を感じさせなかった。まるで心底クラスメイトの身を案じているような温かい言葉を、てらいもなくぽんぽん放ってくる。
lines.english: And he doesn't act as though he's just doing his duty. Warm words tumble out without affectation, as though he truly cares about his classmate.

lines.japanese: 綺麗な花を綺麗と言うのがどこか気恥ずかしい私たちの年代にしては、えらく素直でまっすぐだ。
lines.english: For someone our age, when even calling a pretty flower pretty feels a little embarrassing, he's remarkably honest and straightforward.

lines.japanese: ああ、と私は気付いた。
lines.english: Oh, I realize.

lines.japanese: たぶん、このひとは天然だ。
lines.english: He's probably just naturally guileless.

lines.japanese: 音楽の授業で大まじめに校歌を歌ったって誰にも冷やかされなかった、あの純粋な時代からそのまま育つことが出来たんだろう。
lines.english: He must have managed to grow up unchanged from that innocent time when nobody teased you for singing the school song seriously in music class.

lines.japanese: いいね、と感心する一方で、かわいそうとも思った。世の中の泳ぎ方をある程度知ったとき、きっと過去の自分の朴訥さに身悶えするんだろうな。私がそうだったから。
lines.english: Nice, I think admiringly. But I also feel sorry for him. Once he learns a little about navigating the world, he'll probably writhe at his old, artless self. I did.

lines.japanese: こんな風に考えることがある。人間が立っている座標には、縦や横や高さの他に──そういう既成の概念とはまったく異なる別の「単位」みたいなのがあるんじゃないかと。
lines.english: Sometimes I think this: besides length, width, and height, besides those established concepts, perhaps the coordinates where a person stands have some completely different ‘unit.’

lines.japanese: 緯度でも経度でも高度でもないそれを、私はひそかに明度と呼ぶことにした。たまに濃度とも呼ぶが、しょせん自分語なのでどちらでも問題ない。どのみち辞書的な意味とは一切関係がないのだから。
lines.english: Neither latitude, longitude, nor altitude. Privately, I've decided to call it brightness. Sometimes I call it density, but it's only my own language, so either is fine. It has nothing to do with any dictionary meaning anyway.

lines.japanese: 人間同士が相対するときは、一方または双方がこの明度を調整して、お互いなるべく近似値に保つ必要がある。そうでないと一方または双方がなんとなく「このひととは合わないな」と思うことになる。
lines.english: When people meet, one or both need to adjust this brightness, keeping their values as close as possible. Otherwise, one or both will vaguely feel, ‘I don't get along with this person.’

lines.japanese: 委員長、羽田君は、この「明度」がかなり濃い。だからこういうタイプのひとは、場の明度を見極める目と、自らの明度を落とすすべとを身に付けなければ、たちまち集団の中で浮いてしまう。
lines.english: Our class president, Haneda, has a very dense ‘brightness.’ So unless someone like him learns to gauge the brightness around him and lower his own, he'll immediately stand out in a group.

lines.japanese: ていうか……浮いてるんだろうな。こういうひと、私は嫌いじゃないけど。
lines.english: Or rather... he probably does stand out. I don't dislike people like that, though.

lines.japanese: 元気そうでよかったと邪気のない笑顔を向けられて、私は小さな感動を覚えた。純粋な好意はひとを温かい気持ちにさせる。
lines.english: His guileless smile as he says he's glad I seem well moves me a little. Pure goodwill makes people feel warm.

lines.japanese: じん、と首の後ろあたりに血の巡りのようなものを感じて、それはすうっと首筋を昇り頭の奥をぱっと照らした。
lines.english: I feel something like blood beginning to circulate at the back of my neck. It rises smoothly along my neck and suddenly lights up the depths of my head.

lines.japanese: それが薬の作用なのか、クラスメイトの優しい声によるものなのかは分からない。
lines.english: I don't know whether that's the medicine working or my classmate's kind voice.

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ」
lines.english: “Heh.”

lines.japanese: ともあれ私は笑った。
lines.english: In any case, I smile.

lines.japanese: 羽田タカシ君、か。名前ぐらい覚えておこう。彼にはこのまま、老いゆくまで穢れないでほしい。
lines.english: Takashi Haneda, huh. I should at least remember his name. I hope he stays unspoiled like this right into old age.

lines.japanese: 一方、女子の学級委員も逆の意味で純粋だった。
lines.english: Meanwhile, the girls' class representative is pure in the opposite sense.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、担任に言われたから聞くけど『身体の具合はどうですか』」
lines.english: “Hey, I'm asking because the teacher told me to. ‘How are you feeling?’”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 私が自分の席に着いて、隠れるように澁澤龍彦など読んでいたときである。いかにもセロトニンの足りなそうな顔立ちの高内昌子委員がやってきて告げた。
lines.english: I'm sitting at my desk, hiding behind my reading—some Tatsuhiko Shibusawa—when class representative Masako Takauchi approaches and says this. Her face looks distinctly short of serotonin.

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん……平気……」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah... I'm fine...”

lines.japanese: 呆気に取られて素っ気のない答えになってしまった。しかし高内さんは満足して笑った。
lines.english: Taken aback, I give a curt answer. But Takauchi smiles in satisfaction.

lines.japanese: 「病弱でいいなあ、山科。教師も甘めーもんな。あいつ、私が遅刻したらグチグチ説教かますくせによー」
lines.english: “Must be nice being sickly, Yamashina. Teachers go easy on you. That guy never quits nagging me when I’m late.”

lines.japanese: 「え……ごめん……ていうのも変か。どーしよ」
lines.english: “Uh... sorry... No, that's a weird thing to say. What do I do?”

lines.japanese: 「どーもしなくていいよ、私にゃ関係ねーし。じゃ、お大事に」
lines.english: “You don’t need to do anything. Not my problem. Anyway, take care.”

lines.japanese: 「ありが、とう……」
lines.english: “Thank... you...”

lines.japanese: ひとつも礼を言うようなことはされてないけど、なんとなく頭を下げてしまった。
lines.english: She hasn't done a single thing to thank her for, but somehow I bow my head.

lines.japanese: 彼女といると、どうにも調子が悪い。明度が合わないのだ。
lines.english: Being with her puts me out of sorts. Our brightness doesn't match.

lines.japanese: 対人交流の不首尾は、だいたいこの「明度」の不一致のせいにすれば説明が付いてしまう。そしてその適当な仮説を受けいれれば、自分を悔いたり相手を恨んだりせずに済み、だいぶ気を楽にしてくれる。
lines.english: Most failures in dealing with people can be explained by blaming a mismatch in ‘brightness.’ Accept that convenient hypothesis, and you don't have to blame yourself or resent the other person. It makes things considerably easier.

lines.japanese: 去りかけたあの黒い重力も、ぶり返さずに済む。
lines.english: The dark gravity that was starting to leave needn't come back either.

lines.japanese: 私の人間明度はＫ３６。どこかに波長の合う方いませんか？（てきとう）
lines.english: My human brightness is K36. Anyone out there on my wavelength? (Just a guess.)

lines.japanese: 軽く授業を２コマ受けたら、もうお昼の時間。
lines.english: After just two classes, it's already lunchtime.

lines.japanese: これじゃ高内さんだって皮肉のひとつも言いたくなる──もっとも、彼女は思ったことを口にしただけで、皮肉を言ったつもりじゃないのかもしれないけど。
lines.english: No wonder Takauchi wanted to make a sarcastic remark. Though maybe she was simply saying what she thought, without intending any sarcasm.

lines.japanese: なんとなくいたたまれなくなって、そしてそんな気分でいたらまた沈んでしまうと思って、私は祖母の作ってくれた弁当を鞄に残したまま、混雑する学生食堂へ逃げこんだ。
lines.english: Somehow, I can't bear to stay. Thinking that remaining in this mood would sink me again, I leave my grandmother's packed lunch in my bag and escape into the crowded cafeteria.

lines.japanese: こんなところへひとりで来たって席には着けないのだけど、どのみち食欲はなかった。
lines.english: Coming here alone won't get me a seat, but I don't have an appetite anyway.

lines.japanese: そして、ひとところに落ちついていられる気分でもなかった。胸の奥、心臓のあたりが、疼くようにざわついているのだ。
lines.english: Nor am I in the mood to settle in one place. Something deep in my chest, around my heart, is stirring restlessly, almost aching.

lines.japanese: 例えれば小学生のころの運動会、徒競争の出走直前。あるいは教壇に立たされて作文を読まされる順番待ちの、あのじっとしていられない嫌な感覚。
lines.english: Like the moment before my footrace started at an elementary-school sports day. Or waiting my turn to stand at the teacher's desk and read my essay aloud. That unpleasant feeling of being unable to sit still.

lines.japanese: よくない兆候──これは危惧していたリバウンドだ。指先の感覚が薄くなってきている。まずいなあと思いながら、しかし無意識に歩く速度が上がっていた。
lines.english: A bad sign. This is the rebound I was worried about. The feeling in my fingertips is fading. This isn't good, I think, yet unconsciously, my walking speeds up.

lines.japanese: まずいなあ。まずい、まずい、まずい。
lines.english: This isn't good. Not good, not good, not good.

lines.japanese: 「やましなー！　ぜに貸してー！」
lines.english: “Yamashina! Lend me some cash!”

lines.japanese: そわそわと落ちつきなく歩いていた私に、親しげな声がかけられた。
lines.english: As I walk along restlessly, a friendly voice calls to me.

lines.japanese: あ、渡来さん……。
lines.english: Oh, Watarai...

lines.japanese: 気付いたら噛んでいた親指の爪を下ろして、私は聞きかえした。
lines.english: I lower the thumbnail I find I've been biting and ask again.

lines.japanese: 「お金？」
lines.english: “Money?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……え、ダメ？」
lines.english: “Yeah... Huh, is that a no?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは抱きつくように広げていた両手を、そのまま顔の横に並べてお茶目な笑顔。若手女優みたいな容姿の彼女にそんなことをされると、自然に見えない壁が薄くなってしまう──
lines.english: Watarai keeps both hands, which she'd spread as if to hug me, beside her face and gives a playful smile. When someone who looks like a young actress does that, the invisible wall naturally grows thinner—

lines.japanese: 「なになにどしたのなんでっ？」
lines.english: “What, what happened, why?”

lines.japanese: ──違う。リバウンドのせいで気持ちが少し昂ぶってるんだ。自分のあまり好きじゃない声が出て、思わず一回咳払いした。
lines.english: —no. I'm a little excited because of the rebound. A voice I don't much like comes out of me, and I can't help clearing my throat once.

lines.japanese: 「んんっ」
lines.english: “Ahem.”

lines.japanese: 落ちつけ、落ちつけ。深呼吸、深呼吸。
lines.english: Calm down, calm down. Deep breaths, deep breaths.

lines.japanese: 「なに山科、きょうテンション高いデー？」
lines.english: “What is it, Yamashina? Having a high-energy day?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　うーん、普通かな」
lines.english: “Huh? Hmm... Just a normal day, I guess.”

lines.japanese: めいっぱい普通を意識して答えた。鼓動が速い。落ちつけ、落ちつけ。このひとは洞察力がするどい。落ちついて普通のふりをするんだ。
lines.english: I answer with all my attention on being normal. My pulse is fast. Calm down, calm down. She's perceptive. Calm down and pretend to be normal.

lines.japanese: 渡来さん──２年Ａ組の渡来明日香は、学園一と評される美貌のお姫さま。私とは二年連続で同じクラスだけど、よく話してたのは入学して最初の一ヵ月ぐらいだった。
lines.english: Watarai—Asuka Watarai of class 2-A—is the princess said to be the most beautiful girl in school. We've been in the same class two years running, but we only talked much for the first month or so after starting school.

lines.japanese: あの短いあいだ、何を話していたのかはほとんど思いだせない。そのぐらいどうでもいいことばかりだった。でも意外とつまらなくはなかった。
lines.english: I can hardly remember what we talked about in that brief time. It was all that unimportant. But surprisingly, it wasn't boring.

lines.japanese: 趣味はそんなに合わなかったと思う。部活動も委員会も同じじゃなかった。あのころの私たち、何の話をしてたんだろう。意味もなく心地よかった。きっと明度が近かったんだろう。
lines.english: I don't think our tastes matched very well. We weren't in the same club or committee. What did we talk about back then? It was comfortable for no particular reason. Our brightness must have been close.

lines.japanese: 「山科ってさー」
lines.english: “You know, Yamashina...”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「薔薇の花よりカスミ草が好きでしょ」
lines.english: “You like baby's breath more than roses, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、うん」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「大尺玉より線香花火」
lines.english: “Handheld sparklers over big fireworks.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「マンハッタンよりブルックリン」
lines.english: “Brooklyn over Manhattan.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな自分をカッチョいいと思う」
lines.english: “And you think that makes you cool.”

lines.japanese: 「やな質問」
lines.english: “Mean question.”

lines.japanese: 「違いの分かる自分はカッチョいいと思う」
lines.english: “You think you're cool for knowing the difference.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんってＳだよね」
lines.english: “You're a sadist, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「自分はそこらの有象無象より優れていると思う」
lines.english: “You think you’re better than the faceless masses.”

lines.japanese: 「言うまでもなく、マイナー志向は自己愛の一種だよ」
lines.english: “Obviously, preferring the less mainstream stuff is a form of self-love.”

lines.japanese: （数分間の沈黙）
lines.english: (Several minutes of silence.)

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん」
lines.english: “Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「んー？」
lines.english: “Mm?”

lines.japanese: 「さっき渡来明日香より山科京って言わなかったね」
lines.english: “You didn't say Miyako Yamashina over Asuka Watarai just now.”

lines.japanese: 「何それ、思いもしなかった」
lines.english: “What's that? Never even crossed my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ、うそつき」
lines.english: “Heh. Liar.”

lines.japanese: ああいう文脈のダイアローグがお気に入りだったんだろうな、あの時期の私たちは。
lines.english: We probably liked that sort of dialogue, in that sort of context, back then.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんとは話すことも少なくなってきたけど、今でもまだふたり明度を揃えられるのかな。
lines.english: We don't talk much anymore, but can we still bring our brightness into line?

lines.japanese: 疎遠になった理由は、とくにない。
lines.english: There's no particular reason we drifted apart.

lines.japanese: 強いていえば、学級内で自然発生的なグループが形成される重要な時期──５月ぐらい──に、私が例の発作に見舞われて、他者との交流一切が面倒になってしまったことぐらいか。
lines.english: If I had to name one, it would be that at the important time when groups naturally form in a class—around May—I had one of those attacks, and any contact with others became a burden.

lines.japanese: 「あーいいや、聞いて。あのね、いま私、財布を忘れて深刻な大飢饉なの」
lines.english: “Oh, never mind. Listen. I forgot my wallet, and right now I'm facing a very serious famine.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は胃のあたりを押さえながらきっぱり言った。真剣さと滑稽さが絶妙のバランス。上手いなあ、相手好みの明度へ調整するのが。実に羨ましい。
lines.english: She says it decisively, with a hand around her stomach. A perfect balance of seriousness and absurdity. She's good at adjusting to the brightness the other person prefers. I really envy her.

lines.japanese: 「あした返すから、悪い、５００円貸して」
lines.english: “I'll pay you back tomorrow. Sorry, but lend me five hundred yen.”

lines.japanese: 言葉に甘い色を付けないところもいいなあと思う。だって可愛いひとが可愛い喋り方なんてしたら、それはもうなんていうか……ラフプレイだ。スマートじゃない。
lines.english: I also like that she doesn't sweeten her words. Because if a cute person talks cutely, that's already... playing dirty. Not elegant.

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。ちょっと待って」
lines.english: “Sure. Wait a second.”

lines.japanese: 断る理由もなく、私は喜んで小銭入れを開けた。
lines.english: With no reason to refuse, I happily open my coin purse.

lines.japanese: 「ぃよし！」
lines.english: “Yesss!”

lines.japanese: 彼女も短い歓声をあげ、男の子みたいにこぶしを固めた。釣られてこっちまで笑ってしまう。
lines.english: She gives a little cheer and clenches her fist like a boy. It makes me smile too.

lines.japanese: しかし。
lines.english: However.

lines.japanese: 「あ、残金２１０円」
lines.english: “Oh. I've got 210 yen left.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ」
lines.english: “No way.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんの表情はその一瞬、この世の終焉でも垣間見たような濃い絶望に陰った。
lines.english: For an instant, Watarai's expression darkens with such deep despair you'd think she'd glimpsed the end of the world.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……ええ？　あれ？　なんで」
lines.english: “Sorry... Huh? Wait. Why?”

lines.japanese: 残念だ。せっかく「ありがとう」をもらえるチャンスだったのに。私は諦めきれずにポケットの中をいつまでも探っていた。
lines.english: What a shame. It was a chance to receive a ‘thank you.’ Unable to give up, I keep searching my pockets.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……ごめんね、渡来さん……」
lines.english: “Sorry... I'm sorry, Watarai...”

lines.japanese: 「い、いいよいいよ、気にしないで。べつに私、そこまでお腹すいてたわけでもないんだぁ」
lines.english: “I-it's fine, it's fine. Don't worry. It's not like I was that hungry.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、おかしいの、あるんだよたぶん。だって５００円だよ？　あるでしょ。あるでしょ５００円ぐらい、ぜったいあるって」
lines.english: “No, it's strange. I probably have it. I mean, it's five hundred yen, right? I'd have that. I'd have five hundred yen, wouldn't I? I definitely have it.”

lines.japanese: ああもう……。
lines.english: Oh, come on...

lines.japanese: ああもうっ、なんで無いかなあ。そこは持っとかなきゃ。ああイラッとするなあ。
lines.english: Oh, come on! Why isn't it there? I should have at least that. Oh, this is irritating.

lines.japanese: 「貸さなきゃ、ほんと貸さなきゃ。お金ぐらい貸せるもん、そのぐらい出来るもん。待ってね、ちょっと待ってね、いま手の感覚なくてアレだけど、すぐ見つけるからちょっと待ってね」
lines.english: “I have to lend it to you. I really do. I can lend money. I can do at least that much. Wait, just wait a second. I can't feel my hands right now, but I'll find it in a moment, so just wait.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。そんな、一所懸命あさったって……山科？　山科？」
lines.english: “It's okay. Searching that hard isn't... Yamashina? Yamashina?”
“Huh?!”

lines.japanese: 腕に触れられてはっとした。
lines.english: Her touch on my arm jolts me back.
“Wh-what...?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、なにって」
lines.english: “Well, what do you mean, ‘what’?”

lines.japanese: まずい。やだ……いま私、何してた？
lines.english: Not good. No... What was I doing just now?

lines.japanese: まずいまずい、一秒前の記憶がすっぽり抜けてる。リバウンドの兆候だ。
lines.english: Not good, not good. The memory of a second ago has vanished completely. A sign of the rebound.

lines.japanese: 「私が悪かったよ。ごめん、金欠なのはよく分かったから、そんな必死にアピールしなくても」
lines.english: “My fault. Sorry. I get that you're broke, so you don't have to try so desperately to show it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……うん、うんうん」
lines.english: “Oh... Yeah, yeah, yeah.”

lines.japanese: よかった戻れた。そうだ、渡来さんにお金を貸そうとしたけど、手持ちがなかったんだ。残念。
lines.english: Good. I'm back. Right. I tried to lend Watarai money, but I didn't have enough on me. A shame.

lines.japanese: 私は唇を湿らせてから、改めて会話を再開した。
lines.english: I wet my lips, then begin the conversation again.

lines.japanese: 「こっちこそごめんね、力になれなくて」
lines.english: “I'm sorry too. For not being any help.”

lines.japanese: 「てか、どしたの山科、いま熱っぽいとか？」
lines.english: “Hey, what's up, Yamashina? Are you feeling feverish or something?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　あ、うん、そうなの。ちょっと変でしょ、ぼーっとしてた？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, yeah, that's it. I was a little strange, wasn't I? All out of it?”

lines.japanese: 「や……ぼーっていうか、むしろ、がーって感じ？」
lines.english: “No... More ‘vrrrooom’ than ‘duhhh,’ I’d say?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　ひどーい」
lines.english: “Huh? That's mean.”

lines.japanese: 平然を装って笑いながら、恥ずかしさに逃げだしたくなった。
lines.english: I smile, pretending to be calm, while the embarrassment makes me want to run away.

lines.japanese: 落ちつけ落ちつけ、息を整えよう……うん、正常。
lines.english: Calm down, calm down. Steady your breathing... Yes. Normal.

lines.japanese: 私はまた言葉が溢れでてしまうのが恐くて、珍しくクラスメイトと廊下を並んで歩いたりしているのに、ほとんど自分から口を開くことができなかった。
lines.english: Afraid the words will overflow again, I can hardly bring myself to speak first, even though for once I'm walking beside a classmate in the hallway.

lines.japanese: 暗いやつだと呆れられたのかもしれない。ふだん他の女子や男子と気さくに話しているはずの渡来さんも、やっぱり言葉すくなだった。
lines.english: Maybe she's fed up with how gloomy I am. Watarai, who normally talks so easily with the other girls and boys, doesn't say much either.

lines.japanese: 違うのは顎の角度。私は廊下を行き交う生徒たちの上履きを眺め、彼女は窓の外の白い空を仰いでいた。
lines.english: The difference is the angle of our chins. I watch the indoor shoes of students passing in the hallway. She looks up at the white sky outside the window.

lines.japanese: せっかく私なんかに声をかけてくれた渡来さんのために、彼女の立っている明度に合わせたかった。
lines.english: For Watarai's sake, since she went out of her way to talk to someone like me, I want to match the brightness where she stands.

lines.japanese: だけど私は彼女みたいに器用じゃないから、そう自由には調節できない。
lines.english: But I'm not as skillful as she is. I can't adjust it freely like that.

lines.japanese: 逸る気持ちと速まる心臓の鼓動が、強迫観念のように体の内側を駆けめぐってゆく。
lines.english: My restless feelings and quickening heartbeat race around inside my body like an obsession.

lines.japanese: どく、どく、どく、どく……！
lines.english: Thud, thud, thud, thud...!

lines.japanese: 「今日は走ったら気持ちいいだろうね」
lines.english: “It'd feel good to run today, wouldn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、かもね」
lines.english: “Yeah, maybe.”

lines.japanese: たまに交わされる言葉はその程度のどうでもいい事柄だった。
lines.english: The words we occasionally exchange are about unimportant things like that.
